SMTO-EXE-0105 — SMTO can't show the mouse pointer in screenshots

GUID: b7674aaf-1ff8-565b-ba74-ec00faf28c69
Slug: screen-cursor-unsupported
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • The request asked for a screenshot that shows the mouse pointer, and this version of SMTO can't do that. No screenshot was taken.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send a message asking SMTO to take the screenshot without showing the mouse pointer. Screenshots work normally; only the option to draw the pointer is missing.
  2. If SMTO keeps asking for the pointer, tell it in your message that pointer capture isn't available and it should leave it out. SMTO chose the pointer option itself, so telling it avoids the same refusal.

What success looks like

  • The screenshot appears in the task, without the mouse pointer.

If it still fails

  • If a screenshot without the pointer also fails, that is a different problem: select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • ScreenAdapter.capture rejected include_cursor=true before acquiring any pixels, because this release cannot include the mouse pointer in captures.

What this means

  • Capture received include_cursor true, which the current screen adapter explicitly rejects before pixel acquisition. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Capture received include_cursor true, which the current screen adapter explicitly rejects before pixel acquisition.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the capture request's include_cursor value and whether the pointer is essential to the requested evidence.

How to fix it

  • Call screen.capture with include_cursor=false (the default). Pointer compositing is not implemented in src/gateway_core/platform_screen, and the request was rejected before any capture.
  • Use include_cursor=false. This release captures screen pixels without the mouse pointer.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use include_cursor=false. This release captures screen pixels without the mouse pointer.

How to verify the fix

  • An explicitly accepted cursor-free capture completes, or the unmet cursor requirement is reported.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
